name: Acts

overview.author: Luke the physician, author of the Gospel of Luke and Paul’s travel companion (1:1; the “we” passages from 16:10).
overview.date: About AD 62, since the book ends with Paul under house arrest in Rome awaiting trial.
overview.setting: About AD 30–62, from Jesus’ ascension in Jerusalem through Judea, Samaria, Syria, Asia Minor, Greece, and finally Rome.
overview.purpose: To show how the risen Lord Jesus, by the Holy Spirit, spread the gospel through His witnesses to Jews and Gentiles alike, building one church across every barrier.
overview.structure: Following 1:8: witness in Jerusalem (1–7), in Judea and Samaria (8–12), and to the ends of the earth through Paul’s missionary journeys (13–28).

outline.title: Witness to the Ends of the Earth

items.title: First missionary journey and Jerusalem council
Arrest, trials, and voyage to Rome

themes.title: The Holy Spirit
themes.text: The Spirit empowers, guides, and fills believers.

themes.title: The Resurrection
themes.text: The apostles’ central message is that God raised Jesus.

themes.title: The Church
themes.text: Believers devote themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer.

themes.title: Jews and Gentiles
themes.text: God breaks down barriers and welcomes Gentiles by faith.

themes.title: Suffering and Boldness
themes.text: Persecution spreads rather than stops the gospel.

themes.title: God’s Sovereignty
themes.text: Nothing can hinder the word’s advance, which ends “without hindrance” (28:31).

keyVerses.quote: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses.
And they devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
There is salvation in no one else.
Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.
I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course.

christInBook.text: Jesus ascends and will return in the same way.
God raised Jesus and made Him both Lord and Christ.
Salvation is in no other name.
Stephen sees the Son of Man standing at God’s right hand.
Jesus identifies with His persecuted church: “Why are you persecuting me?”

crossReferences.note: The end of Luke’s first volume.
Paul’s own account of his calling.
The gospel to the Jew first and to the Greek.
Written to churches founded in Acts.

reflection: Where is your “Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and ends of the earth” (1:8)?
How does the early church’s life in 2:42–47 challenge your church life?
Where do you need boldness to speak about Jesus (4:29)?
Which barrier between people might God want to break down through you?
How does Paul’s endurance in suffering encourage you?

chapterList.title: The Ascension
chapterList.summary: Luke recounts Jesus’ 40 days of appearances. Jesus promises the Holy Spirit: “You will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” He ascends, and angels say He will return the same way. The believers pray together, and Matthias replaces Judas.
questions: What is the scope of the mission in 1:8?
What were the disciples doing while they waited (1:14)?
What does the promise of Jesus’ return mean to you (1:11)?

chapterList.title: Pentecost
chapterList.summary: On Pentecost, the Spirit comes with wind and fire, and the disciples speak in other languages. Peter preaches that Jesus, crucified, was raised and exalted, pouring out the Spirit. Cut to the heart, three thousand repent and are baptized. They devote themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer.
questions: How does Pentecost reverse Babel (Genesis 11)?
What were the main points of Peter’s sermon?
What marks the early church community (2:42–47)?

chapterList.title: The Lame Man Healed
chapterList.summary: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth: “I have no silver and gold, but what I do have I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!” Peter explains that faith in Jesus’ name healed him, and calls the people to repent so their sins may be blotted out.
questions: What did Peter and John give the lame man?
How does Peter use the miracle to point to Jesus?
What does “times of refreshing” mean (3:19–20)?

chapterList.title: Boldness Before the Council
chapterList.summary: Peter and John are arrested. Filled with the Spirit, Peter declares, “There is salvation in no one else.” The council notices their boldness and that they had been with Jesus. Threatened, the believers pray for boldness, and the place is shaken. They share everything they have.
questions: What did the council recognize about Peter and John (4:13)?
What did the believers pray for when threatened (4:29)?
How does Barnabas model generosity?

chapterList.title: Ananias, Sapphira, and the Apostles’ Suffering
chapterList.summary: Ananias and Sapphira lie about their gift and fall dead. Great fear comes on the church. Many are healed. The apostles are imprisoned, freed by an angel, and keep preaching: “We must obey God rather than men.” Gamaliel advises caution. The apostles rejoice to suffer for the Name.
questions: Why was Ananias and Sapphira’s sin so serious?
How do the apostles answer the council (5:29)?
How can believers rejoice in suffering (5:41)?

chapterList.title: Seven Chosen to Serve
chapterList.summary: A complaint arises over neglect of Hellenist widows. The apostles devote themselves to prayer and the word, and the church chooses seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom, including Stephen. The word spreads. Stephen is falsely accused before the council.
questions: How did the church solve the conflict?
Why did the apostles prioritize prayer and the word (6:4)?
What qualified the seven to serve?

chapterList.title: Stephen’s Speech and Martyrdom
chapterList.summary: Stephen recounts Israel’s history from Abraham through Moses to the temple, showing that Israel has always resisted the Spirit and rejected God’s messengers. He sees Jesus standing at God’s right hand. He is stoned, praying, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” Saul approves.
questions: What point does Stephen make with Israel’s history?
How does Stephen’s death echo Jesus’ death?
Why is it significant that Saul is mentioned here?

chapterList.title: Philip in Samaria and the Ethiopian
chapterList.summary: Persecution scatters the church, and Philip preaches in Samaria. Many believe, and Peter and John lay hands on them to receive the Spirit. Simon the magician tries to buy the Spirit’s power. Philip explains Isaiah 53 to an Ethiopian official, who believes and is baptized.
questions: How did persecution spread the gospel (8:4)?
What was wrong with Simon’s request?
How did Philip begin with Scripture to explain Jesus (8:35)?

chapterList.title: Saul’s Conversion
chapterList.summary: On the road to Damascus, Saul is struck blind by a light from heaven: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?” Ananias, despite fear, lays hands on him, and he regains sight, is baptized, and preaches Jesus. Barnabas vouches for him in Jerusalem. Peter heals Aeneas and raises Tabitha.
questions: Why does Jesus say Saul is persecuting Him (9:4)?
How does Ananias show courage and obedience?
How did Barnabas help Saul (9:27)?

chapterList.title: Peter and Cornelius
chapterList.summary: Cornelius, a God-fearing centurion, sees a vision telling him to send for Peter. Peter sees a vision of unclean animals: “What God has made clean, do not call common.” Peter preaches at Cornelius’s house, and the Spirit falls on the Gentiles, who are baptized.
questions: What did the vision teach Peter about people (10:28)?
What does 10:34–35 say about God?
Why was the Spirit’s coming on Gentiles so important?

chapterList.title: The Church at Antioch
chapterList.summary: Peter explains the Gentiles’ conversion to critics in Jerusalem, who glorify God. In Antioch, Greeks believe, Barnabas encourages them and brings Saul, and the disciples are first called Christians. They send relief for a famine in Judea.
questions: How did Peter’s critics respond after hearing his account (11:18)?
What made Barnabas a good encourager (11:23–24)?
Why is the name “Christians” significant?

chapterList.title: Peter Freed and Herod’s Fall
chapterList.summary: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter. The church prays earnestly, and an angel leads Peter out. He knocks at Mary’s house, and Rhoda is so happy she forgets to open the gate. Herod accepts worship as a god and is struck dead. The word of God increases.
questions: How did the church respond to Peter’s arrest (12:5)?
Why were the believers surprised when their prayers were answered?
What does Herod’s end teach about pride?

chapterList.title: The First Missionary Journey Begins
chapterList.summary: The Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul. In Cyprus, a magician opposes them and is blinded; the proconsul believes. In Pisidian Antioch, Paul preaches through Israel’s history to Jesus’ resurrection and forgiveness. Jews reject the message, and Paul turns to the Gentiles, who rejoice.
questions: How did the Antioch church discern God’s call (13:2–3)?
What is the core of Paul’s message (13:38–39)?
What does “a light for the Gentiles” mean (13:47)?

chapterList.title: Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe
chapterList.summary: In Iconium, many believe but opposition rises. In Lystra, Paul heals a lame man, and the crowd tries to worship them as gods. Paul points them to the living God. He is stoned and left for dead but rises. They return to strengthen the churches: “Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God.”
questions: How did Paul respond to being treated as a god?
How did Paul speak to people without Scripture (14:15–17)?
Why did Paul return to the cities that hurt him (14:21–23)?

chapterList.title: The Jerusalem Council
chapterList.summary: Some insist Gentiles must be circumcised. The apostles and elders meet. Peter says God saves Gentiles by grace through faith. James cites Amos 9. The council sends a letter not burdening Gentiles with the law, asking them to avoid some practices. Paul and Barnabas separate over John Mark.
questions: What was at stake in the circumcision debate?
How did Peter summarize salvation (15:11)?
How did the church handle disagreement?

chapterList.title: Philippi
chapterList.summary: Timothy joins Paul. The Spirit redirects them; a vision of a Macedonian man calls them to Europe. In Philippi, Lydia believes. Paul casts out a spirit from a slave girl; he and Silas are beaten and jailed. They sing at midnight, an earthquake opens the doors, and the jailer asks, “What must I do to be saved?” “Believe in the Lord Jesus.”
questions: How did God guide Paul through closed doors (16:6–10)?
How could Paul and Silas sing in prison?
What does the jailer’s conversion teach about salvation?

chapterList.title: Thessalonica, Berea, and Athens
chapterList.summary: In Thessalonica, Paul reasons from Scripture and some believe, but a mob forms. The Bereans eagerly examine the Scriptures daily. In Athens, Paul is provoked by idols and speaks at the Areopagus about the “unknown god,” the Creator who calls all people to repent, proving it by raising Jesus.
questions: What made the Bereans “noble” (17:11)?
How did Paul connect with the Athenians’ culture?
How did the Athenians respond to the resurrection?

chapterList.title: Corinth and Ephesus
chapterList.summary: In Corinth, Paul works as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla. God tells him, “Do not be afraid... for I am with you.” He stays 18 months. Apollos, eloquent but incompletely taught, is instructed by Priscilla and Aquila and becomes a strong witness.
questions: How does God encourage Paul in Corinth (18:9–10)?
What do Priscilla and Aquila model about teaching others?
How did Apollos help the church (18:27–28)?

chapterList.title: Ephesus
chapterList.summary: Paul finds disciples who know only John’s baptism; they receive the Spirit. He teaches daily in the hall of Tyrannus for two years. Extraordinary miracles occur. Former magicians burn their books publicly. A riot erupts when silversmiths fear that the gospel threatens Artemis worship.
questions: Why is the Spirit essential to Christian life (19:1–7)?
What does the burning of magic books show about repentance?
Why did the gospel threaten Ephesus’s economy?

chapterList.title: Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
chapterList.summary: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece. In Troas, Eutychus falls from a window during a long sermon and is raised. At Miletus, Paul gives a farewell to the Ephesian elders: he declared the whole counsel of God, warns of wolves, and says, “It is more blessed to give than to receive.”
questions: What does Paul say about his life’s value (20:24)?
What charge does Paul give elders (20:28)?
How does 20:35 apply to your life?

chapterList.title: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
chapterList.summary: Prophets warn Paul of chains in Jerusalem, but he is ready to die for Jesus. In Jerusalem, James advises him to show respect for the law. Jews from Asia stir up a mob, falsely accusing him. Roman soldiers rescue him, and Paul asks to speak to the crowd.
questions: How did Paul respond to warnings of suffering (21:13)?
Why did Paul try to accommodate Jewish believers (21:20–26)?
How does the accusation against Paul mirror Jesus’ treatment?

chapterList.title: Paul’s Defense in Jerusalem
chapterList.summary: Paul tells the crowd his story: zealous persecutor, Damascus road encounter, Ananias’s message, and Jesus’ commission to the Gentiles. At the word “Gentiles,” the crowd erupts. About to be flogged, Paul reveals he is a Roman citizen.
questions: Why is personal testimony powerful?
Why did the word “Gentiles” provoke the crowd?
How did Paul use his citizenship wisely?

chapterList.title: Before the Council and a Plot
chapterList.summary: Paul stands before the Sanhedrin and divides Pharisees and Sadducees over the resurrection. That night the Lord stands by him: “Take courage... you must testify also in Rome.” More than forty men vow to kill Paul, but his nephew exposes the plot, and Paul is sent to Caesarea under guard.
questions: What did the Lord tell Paul (23:11)?
How did God use Paul’s nephew?
How does God work through ordinary circumstances to protect His servants?

chapterList.title: Before Felix
chapterList.summary: The high priest’s lawyer accuses Paul before Governor Felix. Paul defends himself, confessing the Way and hope in the resurrection. Felix, alarmed when Paul speaks of righteousness, self-control, and judgment, delays, hoping for a bribe, and leaves Paul in prison for two years.
questions: How did Paul keep a clear conscience (24:16)?
Why did Felix become alarmed (24:25)?
How can we be tempted to delay responding to God?

chapterList.title: Before Festus: I Appeal to Caesar
chapterList.summary: Festus succeeds Felix. When pressed to go to Jerusalem for trial, Paul appeals to Caesar. King Agrippa and Bernice arrive, and Festus arranges for Paul to speak to them.
questions: Why did Paul appeal to Caesar?
How did God use legal systems to fulfill His promise (23:11)?
What does Festus’s confusion show about how outsiders see the gospel (25:19)?

chapterList.title: Before Agrippa
chapterList.summary: Paul testifies before Agrippa about his conversion and commission to open eyes and turn people from darkness to light. Festus says, “Paul, you are out of your mind.” Agrippa asks, “In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?” Paul wishes all were like him except for his chains.
questions: How does Paul describe his commission (26:16–18)?
How does Paul respond to being called mad?
What does Paul’s response to Agrippa reveal about his heart (26:29)?

chapterList.title: Storm and Shipwreck
chapterList.summary: Paul sails for Rome as a prisoner. Ignoring his warning, they sail into a violent storm. After many days without hope, Paul tells them an angel promised none would die. He urges them to eat. The ship runs aground and breaks up, but all 276 reach land safely.
questions: How did Paul show leadership as a prisoner?
What gave Paul confidence in the storm (27:23–25)?
How does God keep His promises in chaotic circumstances?

chapterList.title: Rome
chapterList.summary: On Malta, Paul survives a viper bite and heals many. He reaches Rome, where believers meet him. He speaks to Jewish leaders, some believing. He lives two years in his own rented house, “proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.”
questions: How does Paul’s survival of the viper show God’s protection?
Why does Paul quote Isaiah 6 (28:25–27)?
Why might Acts end without describing Paul’s trial?

tagline: The risen Jesus continues His work by the Spirit, from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth
readingPlan: 28 chapters: one chapter a day takes 28 days; two a day takes about 14 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
